text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Thursday.
GERMANY - Debt trading in Germany was closed due to a regional holiday. Regular trading in Frankfurt resumes on Friday.

BRITAIN - Gilts sidled into negative territory and, although well placed to outperform, face a volatile market for the next few sessions. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-06/32, down 04/32 from Wednesdays settlement price.

FRANCE - Ignoring uncertainty about the outcome of the French election, 10-year bond futures erased most of their losses to settle just inside negative territory, supported by strong domestic liquidity. The June bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.14, down 0.02 from Wednesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Debt markets held in negative territory as investors freted over the on-going row between the Bundesbank and Bonn on plans to revalue gold reserves which heightened worries over the future of EMU. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.54, down 0.59 from Wednesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury Securities prices maintained a positive tone at midday, boosted by foreign buying and perceptions the ecomony may be slowing. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 109-05/32, up 15/32 from Wednesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 7.0 percent.

JAPAN - Key June 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures recouped early losses to end sharply higher. Weaker- than-expected industrial production data for April released this afternoon triggered hectic buying back, but the topside was capped due to lingering concerns that Japan may raise interest rates some time this year. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.59, up 1.09 from Wednesday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The 10-year dollar sector saw yet another deal launched following British Columbia and Associates Corp on Wednesday, and dealers said there were still further 10-year deals down the road. "The 10-year dollar sector is appealing as it where a lot of investors want to lock in yields in anticipation of a flattening yield curve," a dealer said.
